question.problem:
The force $F,$ measured in newtons $(\text{N})$, needed to extend a spring by some length $l,$ measured in $\text{m},$ is directly proportional to $l.$ When the extension of the spring is $l=0.005\,\text{m},$ the force on the spring is $F=25\,\text{N}.$ What is the constant of variation?

The constant of variation is
{{field-1}}$\text{N/m}.$

current_example.problem: The force $F,$ measured in $\text{kg}\, \text m / \text s^2$, applied to a motorcycle varies directly with its acceleration $a,$ measured in $\textrm{m}/\textrm{s}^2.$ When the acceleration of the motorcycle is $a=5\,\textrm{m}/\textrm{s}^2,$ the force is $F=2\,000\,\text{kg}\, \text m / \text s^2.$ What is the constant of variation?
current_example.worked_solution:
The force $F$ is directly proportional to the acceleration $a,$ so we have

$$
F = k{a},
$$

where $k$ is the constant of variation.

We are told that when the acceleration is $a=5\, \textrm{m}/\,\textrm{s}^2,$ the force is $F=2\,000\,\text{kg}\, \text m / \text s^2.$ We can use this information to solve for $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\,000 & =k\cdot (5) \\ 2\,000 & =5k \\ \frac{2\,000}{5} & =k \\ 400 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since $k = \dfrac{F}{a},$ we have that the units of $k$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{kg m/s}}^{2}}{\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{kg}\cancel{{\text{m/s}}^{2}}}{\cancel{\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2}}} \\  & =\text{kg}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our final answer is $k = 400\,\textrm{kg}.$
